name: Data and Supporting Information for publication "Biostratigraphy and sedimentary sequences of the Toarcian Hainberg section (Northwestern Harz foreland, Northern Germany)" by Arp G. et al., Zitteliana
description: 13 Figures (location map, sections, ammonites, belemnites, stromatolites, stratigraphic scheme), 2 field images, and 2 Tables of geochemical and belemnite data of Lower Jurassic sedimentary rocks (Amaltheenton, Posidonienschiefer, Jurensismergel, Opalinuston) of the Hainberg section (Northern Germany).

citation.name: Arp, G., Balmuk, Y., Seppelt, S. & Reimer, A. (2023): Biostratigraphy and sedimentary sequences of the Toarcian Hainberg section (Northwestern Harz foreland, Northern Germany). - Zitteliana 97: 1–27.

distribution.name: Fig-1-Hainberg-location-map_R1.jpg
distribution.description: Fig. 1. Geographic and geological overview with the location of the Hainberg section and further locations of Toarcian sections in Northern Germany. Outcrop and subsurface deposits of Lower Jurassic after Arnold et al. (1973), Duphorn et al. (1974), Motzka et al. (1979), Waldeck (1986), Kriebel et al. (1998), Motzka-Nöring (1998), Seidel et al. (1998), Radzinski et al. (1999), Knoth et al. (2000), Martiklos (2002), and Reinhold et al. (2008). Supposed former coastlines of the Toarcian after Brockamp (1944; outdated) and Ziegler (1990). Areas outlined in red are Variscan basement rocks, uplifted during the Cretaceous.

distribution.name: Fig-30-Hainberg_Stromatolite_R1.JPG
distribution.description: Figure 30. Thin section micrograph of a stromatolite crust of bed 32, Mactra/Aalensis Subzone, accompanied by marlstone with ooids showing mixed limonitic-calcareous cortices. Note the very dense lamination lacking a fenestral fabric and morphological microbial remains.

distribution.name: Fig-31-Hainberg-adjacent-sections-correlation_R1.jpg
distribution.description: Figure 31. Correlation of the investigated section Hainberg with sections from Northern Germany and Thuringia, with suggested T-R cycles for the sections Hainberg and Dörnten.

distribution.name: Fig-32-Hainberg-adjacent-sections-sequenzstratigraphy_R1.jpg
distribution.description: Figure 32. Sequence stratigraphic interpretation of the Toarcian succession in Northern Germany (including the Hainberg section) and Thuringia in comparison with 3rd order South-German and the 2nd order Boreal standard cycles. Sedimentary succession and ammonite biostratigraphic evidence according to Denckmann (1892), Ernst (1923–1924), Kumm (1941), Ernst (1970), Maul (1984), Brachmann (1991), Krause and Katzung (1999), and specimens from the BGR collection [https://gewis.bgr.de/, leg. K. Hoffmann, R. Jordan, K. Wiedenroth]. T-R cycles: 1 third order sequences Northern Germany (Zimmermann et al. 2015), 2 third order sequences Southern Germany (Röhl and Schmid-Röhl 2005; Arp et al. 2021); 3 second order sequences Boreal standard (de Graciansky et al. 1998; Jacquin et al. 1998).
